clue.text: Slormgorm is pretending to be impressive

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: I am, shortened to I'm
posing means putting on a false identity

explanation.surface: The setter boasts, tongue in cheek, about pretending to be grand.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for 'I', so 'Slormgorm is' gives I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imposing has a grand, commanding appearance that makes a strong impression.

clue.text: With end of trip cancelled, check out and fly?

indicators.note: cancelled says that letter is struck out of the word for check out

parts.note: to inspect is to check out

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of trip

explanation.surface: A traveller cancels the end of a holiday, checks out of the hotel and flies home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb about travel; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly is one example of an insect, a six-legged creature.

clue.text: Dodo-like bird is pea-green and pongs badly

indicators.note: badly says these letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A green-tinged, smelly bird resembling a dodo.
explanation.definitionFit: The passenger pigeon, like the dodo, was a bird hunted to extinction.

clue.text: Drug hit

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to slap or strike

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' also suggests a dose of a drug, joining the two words in one picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for heroin and also means a sharp blow with the open hand.

clue.text: New working benefit creates great difficulty

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on
a plus is a benefit or advantage

explanation.surface: Getting a new job while still claiming benefits causes problems.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, nonplus is a state of perplexity in which one cannot proceed, a great quandary.

clue.text: Thin raised strips in drop-head spanners

indicators.note: drop-head says the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: bridges span rivers, so they are spanners

explanation.surface: Something like car parts: strips on the jaws of spanners in a convertible (drop-head) car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanners' looks like the tools but means bridges; 'drop-head' (a convertible car) tells you to drop the B of BRIDGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridges are narrow raised lines or bands on a surface.

clue.text: Opening time? Flipping vicar gets in Lone Wolf!

indicators.note: gets in says the vicar's letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: an intro is an opening, as of a song

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the vicar's letters are read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title

explanation.surface: A churchman exclaims as he enters at opening time and meets a loner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is a shy, inward-looking person who prefers solitude, like a lone wolf.

clue.text: Docile old genius running Apple

indicators.note: running here means operating, so the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A placid elderly genius is in charge of Apple, the tech company.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised, 'Apple' looks like the computer firm; it is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden Delicious is a popular variety of yellow eating apple.

clue.text: Second article by a conservative related to health

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A news piece about a Conservative politician's health policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanatory means conducive to health, the adjective behind sanatorium.

clue.text: Small mark carried by American bears

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: carried by says one piece is held within another, so the mark goes inside the American letters

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the US
a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: A tiny blemish is being transported by someone from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a load is to bear or support its weight.

clue.text: Red spot probed by first of landers

indicators.note: probed by says something pokes into the word for spot, so a letter goes inside it

parts.note: a stain is a spot

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of landers

explanation.surface: Space news: a red spot on a planet is explored by the first lander craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a colour, as in Jupiter's red spot, but it means a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalin was the Soviet communist leader, and a Red is a communist.

clue.text: In hearing, those who vote for studies

indicators.note: in hearing says the word is taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the ayes are those voting yes in Parliament

explanation.surface: At a court hearing, the supporters review the evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, so eyes means studies, as a verb.

clue.text: Lip or another part of the body

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the side of the face below the eye

explanation.walkthrough: Lip is itself a body part, which makes 'another part' read like a list, but here lip means sauce or impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both impertinent talk and the fleshy side of the face.

clue.text: A sly otter on the loose in Bury

indicators.note: an animal on the loose runs free, so these letters are free to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cunning otter has escaped in the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury reads as the Lancashire town, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay someone to rest is the idiom for burying them after death.

clue.text: Laments crossing through a river in waders

indicators.note: crossing through means striking out, so the river letter is deleted

parts.note: regrets means laments, as verbs
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone grieves while wading across a river in fishing boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waders' looks like rubber boots; it means birds that wade.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are long-legged herons that stalk through shallow water, so they are wading birds.

clue.text: Old judge locks up individual free of blame

indicators.note: locks up says the outer pieces enclose the individual

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to rate is to judge or assess
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A retired judge jails someone who is innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone of an accusation, declaring them blameless.

clue.text: Slight rainfall ultimately disrupts transmitter

indicators.note: disrupts says the letter breaks into the word for transmitter

parts.note: a sender is something that transmits

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of rainfall

explanation.surface: A little rain eventually interferes with a radio mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender or slight figure is thin and small in build.

clue.text: Surprisingly, you must punch fake friend

indicators.note: must punch says the letter for you breaks into the other pieces

parts.note: to act is to pretend or fake
an ally is a friend
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: An instruction to hit a false friend, amazingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Actually is used to introduce something unexpected, as in 'actually, it worked', meaning surprisingly or in fact.

clue.text: Forcibly remove aristocrat sat on motor

indicators.note: sat on places the aristocrat on the motor, so the aristocrat comes after it

parts.note: a motor is British slang for a car
a toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A posh person perched on a car is being dragged away by force.
explanation.definitionFit: To cart someone off is the idiom for taking them away against their will.

clue.text: One caught in the Penguin's trap at Gotham Zoo?

definitions.text: One caught in the Penguin's trap at Gotham Zoo?

parts.words: One caught in the Penguin's trap at Gotham Zoo?
parts.note: the Penguin is Batman's villain, but a real zoo penguin's trap is its beak, and what it catches is its dinner

explanation.walkthrough: The Penguin is the Batman villain from Gotham City; 'trap' is slang for mouth, so a zoo penguin's trap catches its food.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguins feed on fish, the sea creatures they catch in their beaks.

clue.text: Fly, but not low, in vessel

indicators.note: but not says the following word is taken away from the fly

parts.note: a bluebottle is a large blowfly
feeling low is feeling blue

explanation.surface: An insect, not flying low, is in a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb but it is the insect, BLUEBOTTLE; 'not low' removes BLUE, the word for feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle is a container for liquids, and vessel is a general word for such a container.

clue.text: Can able criminal be in equilibrium?

definitions.note: a verb phrase, matching the verb sense of the answer

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether a capable crook can stay steady.
explanation.definitionFit: To balance is to stay steady with forces evenly matched, a state of stable poise.

clue.text: This sedan partly leaked gas noisily

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A car with a punctured tyre or faulty pipe whistling as gas escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas escaping through a small hole makes a sibilant whistling sound.

clue.text: Catholic cook ruins veal

indicators.note: to cook is to alter or doctor, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy chef spoils the veal.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised, 'Catholic' suggests the church; uncapitalised it means all-embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic in its lower-case sense means wide-ranging, applying to everyone, which is what universal means.

clue.text: Very cold hotel, one in foreign resort

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
C is the tap abbreviation for cold
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A traveller complains about a freezing hotel at an overseas holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Sochi, on Russia's Black Sea coast, hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics, so 'very cold' fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sochi is a Russian seaside town and winter sports venue, a holiday destination abroad.

clue.text: Southern centre welcomes republican Bush

indicators.note: welcomes says the centre takes in the republican letter

parts.note: a hub is a centre

explanation.surface: A Southern convention welcomes Republican president George Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the US president, as the republican suggests; it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant smaller than a tree, another word for a bush.

clue.text: Song written about drugs with Space

indicators.note: written about says the song is set down around the other letters

parts.note: a lay is an old word for a song or ballad
E is slang for the drug ecstasy, so two of them make drugs

explanation.surface: A rock song is composed about drug-taking and outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to manoeuvre, a margin of freedom, which is what space means here.

clue.text: Super-sized moon sure looks different

indicators.note: if something looks different its form has changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A supermoon certainly appears unlike its usual self.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means very large, the same as super-sized.

clue.text: American jerk's extremely execrable

parts.note: to yank is to jerk, as nouns

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme ends, the first and last letters, of execrable

explanation.surface: An American idiot is said to be utterly awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' reads as an insult but means a sudden pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is an informal name for a person from the United States.

clue.text: As one could describe some spiders online?

definitions.text: As one could describe some spiders
definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: living on a web
second meaning: operating over the internet

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the hyphenated word means based on a web, as a spider is; in its usual sense it means run over the World Wide Web.
explanation.definitionFit: Services delivered through the internet are described as operating on the World Wide Web.
